Buy fewer games, and of those you own, keep a limited amount installed on your system.

Yeah, I know that sounds weird, but I bought tons of games through bundles and sales and never played them. They just piled up into a huge list on my Steam Library and each addition just made it harder to pick what to play. I'd end up staring at my list more than playing, and even when I did, it was usually something I'd played many times before.

Then I realized I was wasting my money because the deals seemed like a good idea, but I was never actually using any of what I was buying. It didn't matter that I was buying 5-6 games for ten bucks if I ended up only playing the first level or two of one of them most of the time and spent more time staring at the list trying to figure out what to play rather than actually playing anything.

However, I did notice that some games I actually did end up playing. Fallout 4 for example has kept me occupied for quite some time now. I knew I was going to play it. It wasn't something I picked up because I got it cheap on a sale, it was something I anticipated and knew I would play all the way through. These games are the ones I keep coming back to when I actually do decide to play something most of the time.

I realized that games I do this with are rarely a surprise to me. 99% of the time I know they are coming and that I will be spending time with them before they are released. I'm not talking about franchise games necessarily either. I know what styles of games are more likely to hold my attention. If I'm not sure, I wait until reviews are out. I very rarely actually buy games at launch or as a preorder anymore, and only on titles I know already have me sold and that I'll play. I bought GTA V as a pre-order for example, because I knew I was going to buy and play it no matter what anyone said about it.

I cleaned out a lot of stuff from my PC and now only actually have a few games that actually interest me installed. I still have that massive list on Steam if I just open my library, but the installed option when you right click on Library narrows it down a lot. I no longer buy games because they mildly interest me and happen to be on sale. More often than not, I don't play them when I do that and they end up ignored.

Fewer options eliminate that staring at the huge list choice overload and I actually end up playing more. Once I finish with a game, outside of a few I know I'll play repeatedly, I uninstall it.

There are a few standby's I keep on the drive that I actually use sometimes. Doom and Fallout being good examples. Most stuff, I might think for a bit that I might decide to play again one day, but chances are I won't. I've been biting the bullet and just getting rid of them, reducing my list down to about 15-20 installed games at a time, several of which are old favorites that I already mentioned.

Franchise games I also force myself to uninstall. As much as I like San Andreas and GTA IV, I'm probably not going to play either again now that GTA V is out. Same goes for Oblivion since Skyrim was released. Yeah, I know I can mod those games, but I can also Mod Skyrim and if I'm going to bother that's probably what I'll realistically do. I had tons of fun with them, and I might actually reinstall them and play them again one day, but chances are, I'll be fine with them off my HDD until I do.

It's also worth mentioning that if you buy a game and end up not liking it as much as you thought you might, just get rid of it. Don't think 'maybe I'll come back to it when I'm done with some of the stuff I'm more interested in' just uninstall it and accept that it wasn't what you expected and didn't interest you. You will never come back to it, there will always be something else you're more interested in that will keep you from going back to it. Accept it as sunk cost and move on.

At the end of the day, the less bloated your game library is, the more likely you are to actually pick something out and play it. You do want a few options, but keep it down to a reasonable number of choices. Give yourself about fifteen to twenty slots and rotate games out when you get something new.

Keep about a quarter of that reserved for favorite titles that you know you'll come back to. Minecraft, Doom, Fallout, Elder Scrolls, Wing Commander, whatever MMO has your attention, Diablo, whatever. PIck a few that hold your interest and leave them, but everything else should be rotated out. Don't buy something new unless you're willing to take something older out of the lineup and stick to that. It will be hard at first and you'll have to force yourself to rip some of the stuff out, but take comfort that it's still in your library and that you can always rotate it back in if you find you really do want to play it.

Since I started doing this, I've found myself playing a lot more often and finishing more games. When I beat something, unless it's one of those very special games I know I'll keep coming back too, it gets cleaned off my drive, opening up another space for something new.

This might sound weird, but you might be surprised how much more often you actually play when you clear out the noise of the junk titles that just happened to be cheap from your system.

Another addition I'd add to this, is don't give games a pass for being small.

Don't think "It's just a few MBs I'll just leave it".

Those little titles are just as much a distraction and waste of space as the big ones.

The same goes for the opposite. Don't think "I don't want to have to download all this again". If you're not playing it, it's a waste of space.

Size matters not. A game you're not playing is a game you're not playing, no matter how much drive space it takes up, and it's just another name on the list that distracts from actually making a choice about what to play.
